title: On‑Prem Firewall Policy Drift — Tactical Incident Notes & Runbook Draft
content:
Summary:

Short incident summary: On 2026-01-17 at ~03:45 UTC a subset of customer on-prem clusters hosted in Region E (customer-managed firewalls) lost steady control-plane connectivity to Redwood control endpoints. Symptoms included periodic heartbeat timeouts, k8s node status flapping from "Ready" to "NotReady", and automated failover/reconnect cycles that increased request latency and triggered a number of canary rollbacks on Dedicated routing. Impact was limited to 7 clusters across 3 customers; customer workloads continued to serve read-only traffic but write/coordination paths degraded.

High-level root cause (short): A policy-as-code automated sync pushed a translated firewall template that unintentionally inserted deny rules for the control-plane CIDR/ports (8443 and 443) due to variable interpolation mismatch between vendor templates and the customer's policy repo. The result was intermittent blocking for short TCP windows, which manifested as TCP RSTs and connection timeouts at application health-check granularity.

Timeline (UTC):
- 2026-01-17 03:42 — First alert: health-check failures from monitor-poller for control-plane endpoint cp-prod-e1.redwood.net (alert INC-2026-0012 created).
- 2026-01-17 03:45 — On-call SRE (Asha) gets PagerDuty. Initial triage shows 5 clusters with elevated control-plane latency and 3 with heartbeat timeouts.
- 2026-01-17 03:50 — Customer ops Slack thread shows a recent automated policy sync completed at 03:38 from their internal CI job (repo: infra-firewall-rules).
- 03:55 — We request a tcpdump and iptables/nft output from customer environment. They confirm an extra DENY rule applied to INPUT chain referencing control-plane CIDR (10.240.10.0/24) and port 8443.
- 04:05 — Mitigation: customer adds a temporary ACCEPT rule placed above the deny and flushes conntrack entries for control-plane IPs. Heartbeats recover within 90s on most clusters.
- 04:22 — Full recovery observed; alerts resolve.
- 2026-01-18 — Post-incident investigation begins; initial notes collected.

Detection & Monitoring Notes:
- Primary detector: control-plane health-check probe (every 15s) and node status change alerts.
- Secondary signals: increased 5xx errors on internal control-plane APIs, elevated latency in routing telemetry, and number of connection resets (observed in tcpdump as TCP RSTs).
- Gaps: We did not have a dedicated alert for "sudden presence of new firewall deny rules" (obviously outside our managed infra). We relied on downstream degradation observability.

Investigation (what we looked at and key commands):
- Requested from customer: sudo iptables -S (or nft list ruleset), sudo iptables -L -n -v, sudo conntrack -L | grep <control-ip>.
- Captured tcpdump on customer's edge box: tcpdump -nn -i eth0 host 10.240.10.12 and port 8443 -w cp-8443.pcap (sample showed SYN followed by RST within 200ms in failure windows).
- Verified control-plane side logs: repeated connection attempts from cluster egress IPs with immediate remote RSTs.
- Cross-checked recent CI runs: customer CI job id 7842 (policy-sync) completed 03:38 with template translation step using tool 'fw-translate v2.1' which had a recent change (PR 77) altering placeholder semantics.

Root cause analysis (detailed):
- Immediate cause: A deny rule matching control-plane CIDR and port was inserted by the customer's policy sync. Rule ordering caused it to be evaluated before previously-existing allows. Because the deny was intermittent (was applied during partial sync and then reordered by another automation step), some packets passed while others failed, resulting in intermittent TCP resets and timeouts.
- Contributing factors:
  - Vendor translation tool changed placeholder substitution semantics in a minor release; the customer's CI did not pin the translation tool version nor run a dry-run check that asserted rule equivalence.
  - The customer's policy-as-code pipeline applied changes atomically across many devices but did not have a preflight simulation that checks control-plane reachability.
  - Our monitoring assumed persistent reachability loss for full outage alerts; intermittent RSTs generated multiple noisy signals and triggered cascading automated mitigations (some canary rollbacks).

Immediate mitigations taken (workarounds):
- Customer inserted a temporary high-priority ACCEPT for control-plane (iptable insert -I INPUT 1 -s 10.240.10.0/24 -p tcp --dport 8443 -j ACCEPT) on affected nodes and flushed related conntrack entries.
- We advised rate-limit relaxation on control-plane health-check retries for 10m to avoid thrashing of auto-rollouts.
- Extra logging enabled on control-plane ingress to capture any future RST/ICMP unreachable patterns.

Permanent fixes recommended (short-term roadmap):
1) Customer recommended changes (owner: Customer-NOC):
   - Pin version of translation tool (fw-translate) and add a pre-deploy lint that fails on any DENY rule matching Redwood control-plane CIDR/ports.
   - Add a preflight connectivity check step in policy CI that performs a TCP connect to control-plane endpoints from representative egress IPs.
   - Change deployment pipeline to apply rule changes in a safe ordering model: ensure explicit allow entries for control-plane exist before any deny rules referencing broad CIDRs are enabled.

2) Redwood-side changes (owners: eng-sre-private-deployments + product-hosted-api):
   - Add a dedicated synthetic check (every 30s) measuring port-level TCP handshake success rate for control-plane endpoints from customers' egress blocks where allowed, with a low-latency alert on sudden spike in RST or SYN-ACK failures. (Owner: Evan Zhou, timeframe: 2 weeks)
   - Create a "reachability-exemption" spec for private deployments that customers can opt into to mark control-plane ports as protected from automated deny templates. (Owner: Priya Menon, timeframe: 1 month)
   - Publish a guidance doc for customers: "Policy-as-code safe deploy checklist" that highlights ordering, pinning translators, and simulations. (Owner: Solutions Eng, timeframe: 3 weeks)

Runbook draft for on-call (candidate procedure for similar incidents):
- Triage phase (first 10 minutes):
  1. Confirm scope: check monitoring dashboard for clusters impacted, list of customer clusters, and ingress/egress IPs.
  2. Run control-plane connect test from our tracing agent and request immediate tcpdump/iptables output from customer if on-prem: commands provided below.
  3. If customers report recent policy CI runs within last 30 minutes, flag potential policy drift and ask to pause automatic syncs.

- Investigation commands to request from customer (copy-paste):
  - sudo iptables -S | sed -n '1,200p'
  - sudo nft list ruleset (if nft in use)
  - sudo iptables -L -n -v | grep -i 8443
  - sudo conntrack -L | grep <control-plane-ip>
  - sudo tcpdump -nn -i <edge-if> host <control-ip> and port 8443 -c 200 -w /tmp/cp-8443.pcap

- Quick workaround steps to advise (only if customer consents):
  1. Insert an ACCEPT rule above the deny (iptables -I INPUT 1 -s <control-cidr> -p tcp --dport <port> -j ACCEPT).
  2. Flush conntrack entries for the control-plane IPs: sudo conntrack -D -d <control-ip> -p tcp.
  3. Pause policy sync jobs and roll back the last CI change that introduced the template translation.

- When to escalate:
  - If issue affects >20% of customer clusters or triggers cross-region control-plane errors, escalate to SRE manager and product oncall.
  - If mitigation cannot be applied within 30 minutes due to lack of customer access, open C-level customer communication and involve Solutions Eng.

On-call quick reference (cheat sheet):
- Control-plane ports: 8443 (primary), 443 (fallback management).
- Quick TCP test (Redwood agent): curl -s -v --connect-timeout 2 https://<control-ip>:8443/healthz to check handshake and TLS.
- Conntrack cleanup: conntrack -D -d <control-ip>

Post-incident action items (owners & due dates):
- Customer: pin fw-translate version and add preflight connectivity check — Customer-NOC — due 2026-02-05.
- Redwood SRE: implement synthetic port-level check and alerting — Evan Zhou — due 2026-02-01.
- Redwood Product: draft reachability-exemption spec and publish docs — Priya Menon — due 2026-02-15.
- Solutions Eng: update customer onboarding checklist to include policy-as-code guidance — Luca Bianchi — due 2026-02-08.
- Engineering: add a small test harness in infra repo to simulate policy translations and detect DENY insertions for protected CIDRs — PR #4127 (see linked) — due 2026-02-10.

Retrospective notes / things learned:
- Even when infrastructure is customer-managed, we must assume policy-as-code automation will be a frequent source of incidents and proactively provide guardrails.
- Small changes in third-party translation tools can have outsized impact; pinning versions and adding minimal simulation tests is low-effort, high-value.
- Intermittent packet-level failures are harder to detect than total blackouts; we should have alerts tuned to spikes in TCP RSTs and SYN failure ratios.

Appendix A — Example messaging to customer (short template):
"We observed transient control-plane connectivity issues originating around 03:38 UTC. Our investigation indicates a recent policy-sync job may have introduced a deny rule that affected ports used by the control plane. Recommended immediate action is to insert a temporary allow rule for <control-cidr>:8443, flush related conntrack entries, and pause policy syncs while we validate the policy template. We can provide the specific iptables/nft commands if you want us to run them together with your team."

Appendix B — Raw on-call notes (sanitized):
- 03:46 — Asha: got PD, pinged customer NOC and asked for iptables output.
- 03:48 — Customer: CI job 7842 ran at 03:38, logs show fw-translate v2.1 executed.
- 03:52 — Asha: requested tcpdump; customer uploaded pcap showing RSTs.
- 03:58 — Customer: inserted accept rule, flushed conntrack.
- 04:00 — Most clusters heartbeats recovered.
- 04:22 — All alerts cleared.

Status: document is a working draft intended to become the canonical SRE runbook for firewall-policy drift incidents affecting on-prem private deployments. Feedback welcome; want to validate runbook steps with Solutions Eng and Customer-NOC before marking final.

"End of document."
